hook_text: Your model is finished. Now the hardest part: finding out, honestly, whether it works, with numbers.
clip_script: Evaluation is judging on evidence, not hope. Four words. Objective: set the tests first, write results as they happen, verdict last. Fair: judge it against its own brief, weaknesses as loud as strengths. Accurate: numbers with units, repeated; 520 grams, 70 degrees, 30 minutes, base soft, no leak. In depth: past the object to the real rank. Test every rule in a four-column table, and write the fails plainly: walls buckled at 14, rib only touched the base. That line is your best recommendation. Then back to the brief: less harm, same benefit, works with no water or bins? And be honest about your own product's footprint, because harm moved is not harm removed. End with numbered fixes. A team that admits two fails and explains them beats a team that claims seven passes.
visual_style: Kitchen scale reads 520 g; stopwatch runs; a stack of containers crushes at 14 with a red line; a four-column table fills with ticks, a cross and a reason; three arrows back to the brief; a footprint icon on the new product.
pacing: Four words, the table, the fail recorded, back to the brief, footprint, fixes.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write one test for your model with the number you will measure.
